Research_Question: Do structural refactoring commits exhibit different test-level missed-failure behavior in history-based ML-PTS models compared to standard feature commits?
Hypothesis: Refactoring category is associated with differences in PTS test-level missed-failure behavior.
Falsification_Condition: The test-level miss behavior for refactoring commits is statistically indistinguishable from feature commits.

Research_Question: Which specific categories of structural refactoring (e.g., class renames, method moves, cross-module extractions) are most strongly associated with differences in PTS false negatives?
Hypothesis: Identity-changing refactorings exhibit larger changes in PTS input features than refactorings that preserve historical identity.
Falsification_Condition: Identity-preserving refactorings exhibit the same or higher feature distribution shift and miss behavior as identity-changing refactorings.

Research_Question: To what extent is the refactoring-associated change in PTS performance attenuated when historical code identity is preserved through structural mapping?
Hypothesis: Preserving structural identity reduces missed-failure behavior if the failure is caused by representation shift.
Falsification_Condition: Identity-aware PTS interventions (e.g., mapping renamed files) result in the same or higher test-level miss behavior compared to the baseline model.
